market_read: Six live comparables were found, three of them charging real, published, low prices for materially the same 'Kalshi/Polymarket historical tape, queryable' product our raw kx_history.py archive access would be: kalshibacktest.com Pro at $19.90/mo (Kalshi crypto order-book, 31-day paid window), pmxt.dev Starter/Pro at $29.99/$99.99/mo (multi-venue metered API), kingsets.com free-only (30-day CSV/BigQuery). The underlying trade archive itself (TrevorJS/kalshi-trades, HuggingFace, CC-BY-4.0, verified in this repo's DATA_SOURCES.md) is FREE and already publicly downloadable with no signup. That means the raw-data layer is a commodity with a price ceiling near $0-20/mo set by live competitors and one genuinely free incumbent -- selling raw tape access head-on is a bad business per the orchestrator's own kill rule. The sellable layer, if any, is validated correctness and reconciliation, not access.

gaps_identified.gap: Settlement-truth reconciliation as a discrete, citable service
gaps_identified.evidence_none_of_the_comparables_serve_i: None of the six comparables' public pages mention validating trade/backtest outcomes against Kalshi's official settlement `result` field. This repo has direct, embarrassing proof of why that matters: PAPER_TRADER_AUDIT.md found 14.2% of a prior sleeve's SELF-SCORED outcomes were wrong when checked against `GET /trade-api/v2/markets/{ticker}` -> `result` (cited in DATA_SOURCES.md sec 3). verify_settlement_truth.py and out/settlement_truth.json already exist as the tooling that catches this class of bug.
gaps_identified.who_would_pay: Third-party quant researchers / backtest-framework builders who compute their own market outcomes (from price thresholds, brackets, etc.) instead of pulling Kalshi's official settlement field -- exactly the mistake this program already made and caught internally.

gaps_identified.gap: Full-fidelity (16/16 shard) + bid/ask (not last-trade-only) + archive-to-live-bridged research dataset
gaps_identified.evidence_none_of_the_comparables_serve_i: kalshibacktest.com Pro caps paid history at 31 days; kingsets.com caps free access at 30 days; the free CC-BY HuggingFace archive itself was, until this repo's own bugfix (DATA_SOURCES.md sec 1a), silently missing 7 of 16 trade shards (44% of the tape) in the naive reading every downstream consumer would plausibly reproduce -- and even fixed, the archive is frozen at 2026-01-28 with a ~6-month hole vs. today that only the candlestick-bid/ask bridge (already built, used in PAPER_TRADER_AUDIT.md) fills.
gaps_identified.who_would_pay: Same audience as above -- a narrow, technically sophisticated slice of independent Kalshi quant researchers, likely dozens to low hundreds of people total, not a mass market.

gaps_identified.gap: The 42-study graveyard as a published, adversarially-verified negative-results research record
gaps_identified.evidence_none_of_the_comparables_serve_i: All six comparables sell DATA ACCESS. None publish RESEARCH FINDINGS (what does/doesn't work, and why, with the kill mechanism named). This program has a genuinely unusual asset: 42 pre-registered strategies, each independently re-run/re-verified (2 blind builds + adversarial Fable review gate per MAKER_VIABILITY.md), all killed and documented with the specific statistical mechanism (nonstationarity, achievability, stale-print artifact, etc.). This is closer to a sell-side quant research product (which normally costs five or six figures/yr, e.g. institutional research subscriptions) than to a data feed, and nothing comparable exists in the public Kalshi/Polymarket tooling space found in this search.
gaps_identified.who_would_pay: Prospective Kalshi algo-traders (individuals or small funds) deciding whether to spend months rediscovering that maker/resting-bid capture, favorite-longshot fade, and latency racing on crypto up/down are all dead ends on this venue -- a real but small and price-sensitive audience.

opportunities_ranked.type: CONTENT/PUBLICATION -- zero fill risk, zero quoting obligation, ships from files already on disk
opportunities_ranked.mechanics: Publish the existing kill reports (MAKER_VIABILITY.md, ref/RESEARCH_LEDGER.md graveyard table, and the underlying methodology write-ups) as a structured, citable research record -- e.g. a static site or newsletter, one entry per killed strategy with the specific mechanism, the pre-registered bar, and the verification chain (2 blind builds + adversarial review). dead_ends.idea: Sell raw/bulk access to the 16-shard Kalshi trade archive (kx_history.py) as a subscription data product
dead_ends.why_killed: Competes head-on with a free incumbent by the orchestrator's own rule: the underlying TrevorJS/kalshi-trades archive is CC-BY-4.0, free, no signup, directly downloadable from HuggingFace (verified, DATA_SOURCES.md sec 1). It is also underpriced by two live competitors doing materially the same thing: kalshibacktest.com Pro at $19.90/mo and kingsets.com free-only. Our only real edge (the 9-vs-16 shard bugfix) fixes a bug in reading a FREE dataset -- it is a documentation/correctness contribution to the commons, not a moat; anyone else who reads the archive's own file listing finds the same 16 shards.

dead_ends.idea: BRTI-reconstruction as a paid always-on reference-price WS feed for other Kalshi crypto traders
dead_ends.why_killed: Fails the >20h/mo maintenance ceiling on inspection: ENGINEERING_STACK.md sec 4 documents that CF Benchmarks' BRTI methodology is 'a living spec... changed twice in the 10 weeks before measurement' and requires 'a version-tracking chore, not a one-time build,' on top of the uptime/support burden of running a paid always-on feed (monitoring, incident response, customer SLA) for a tiny, technical, low-volume customer base. The underlying constituent feeds (Coinbase, Kraken, Bitstamp, Gemini) are themselves free and directly usable by any sophisticated customer, further compressing willingness to pay.

dead_ends.idea: Sell the sub-3ms execution stack itself (colocation-equivalent placement, warm-process pattern, queue-position tooling) as white-label infrastructure/SaaS for other Kalshi bot builders
dead_ends.why_killed: The stack was built and measured specifically to serve a maker strategy that failed its own registered kill gates (MAKER_VIABILITY.md) -- selling 'the infrastructure for a strategy we ourselves killed' to third parties is an integrity problem before it is a business-viability problem (we would be marketing infra whose own economic overlay says 'no infrastructure spend is justified by any currently-validated strategy,' ENGINEERING_STACK.md line 20-21). Even setting that aside, this is bespoke devops consulting per customer, not a productized SKU -- high variable cost, small addressable market, does not meet 'minimum compliance cost' scoped by this task.

us_person_note: Every opportunity in this file is a US-legal content/service business built on Kalshi's own public official API and a CC-BY-licensed public dataset -- no geo-blocking issue exists (that is specifically a global-Polymarket problem noted elsewhere in this repo, e.g. FINDINGS.md). No trading, no order placement, no quoting obligation, and therefore none of these opportunities are priced against MAKER_VIABILITY.md's maker-fill cost bounds -- that cost model does not apply because nothing here takes a fill.
bottom_line: Six live public comparables (kalshidata.com, kingsets.com, pmxt.dev, polymarketanalytics.com, kalshibacktest.com, lycheedata.com) already sell materially the same 'Kalshi/Polymarket historical data, queryable' product this stack could offer, at prices from free to $99.99/mo, on top of an underlying archive that is itself free and CC-BY-licensed. That collapses the obvious 'sell the archive' idea into a dead end. The two things genuinely not served by any comparable found -- a citable record of 42 adversarially-verified negative results, and bounded settlement-truth audits using tooling that already caught a real 14.2% error rate in this program's own prior work -- are real gaps, but both are small-audience, low-absolute-revenue plays (ESTIMATE: low hundreds of $/mo combined, not a business), not a pivot that replaces the trading program. Their appeal is asymmetric: near-zero build cost (content and tooling already exist), near-zero maintenance, and zero quoting/fill risk -- consistent with the task's 'minimum compliance cost' framing, but the ceiling should be stated honestly rather than dressed up.
